issues.description: URL construction complects parsing, arch detection, and path assembly into one ad-hoc transform
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only takes a URL string, splits on '/', regex-scans for arch, and rebuilds a path — three concerns intertwined with no intermediate value. The fact about each package (name, version, release, arch, source-repo) is the value; the URL is a rendering. Parse once into a typed record (a dict), then render. Right now arch detection and NEVRA extraction are coupled to URL shape, and any future repo path change breaks both.

issues.description: nevra[0].lower() assumes the filename starts with an ASCII letter — silent breakage waiting
issues.detail: The koji path uses the first letter of the package name, but nevra here is the full filename like 'kernel-6.8-1.fc40.x86_64.rpm'. nevra[0] happens to work, but it's an unstated invariant: the value being indexed is a filename, the key being derived is package-name-initial. Name the value. Otherwise a package starting with a digit or non-ASCII char produces a malformed path with no error.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returning None is silently swallowed into a broken URL
issues.detail: If the regex misses, arch becomes None and the f-string produces '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. No fact about the world says 'this arch is unknown' — it just propagates as a string 'None'. Either make arch a required value (raise) or model 'unknown arch' explicitly. Right now the caller has no way to distinguish success from failure, and a downstream 404 is the only signal.

issues.description: The race condition and 'safe to craft URL prior to availability' is essential, not incidental, complexity left undocumented in code
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges a race between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger tagging. That's a real time-semantics claim: 'this URL will exist later.' The code asserts it silently. A one-line comment naming the invariant ('these URLs are valid only after coreos-koji-tagger runs against this commit') keeps the time model explicit instead of tribal.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list duplicates knowledge already present elsewhere in the tool
issues.detail: The arches list ['x86_64','aarch64','ppc64le','s390x'] is a value about the world (which arches CoreOS targets) embedded in a regex helper. get_basearch is already imported. If the supported arch set changes, this function won't know. Pull the arch set to a single named value and pass it in, or derive it from the same source the rest of the pipeline uses.

review.summary: The patch fixes a real DNF5 bug by rewriting non-coreos-pool URLs to a canonical koji path, but the rewrite complects URL parsing, arch detection, and path templating into one string-in/string-out function with implicit invariants. The values flowing through (NEVRA, arch, repo-origin) should be parsed into a record once and rendered once, not pattern-matched ad hoc. Silent failure modes (arch=None producing 'None' in the URL, nevra[0] assuming an ASCII letter) trade a known bug for harder-to-detect ones. The time-semantics claim — 'this URL will be valid after koji-tagger runs' — is the essential complexity here and deserves to be named in the code, not just the commit message. EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: the fix works but accretes incidental complexity around a problem the upstream DNF5 bug created.
